summary:
WP2 is implemented and every acceptance test AT2.1–AT2.16 passed in real runs. That includes all the [gated] ones: WP1's core gate functions already exist in the shared tree, so the gated tests ran against WP1's in-progress code instead of skipping.

What was built:
1. The run shadow (packages/runner/src/shadow/): a working copy `ws/` holding only model and project files, and a separate build copy `build/` where Lean runs, seeded from the user's `.lake/build`. Symlinks and special files in the user's tree or in `.lake/build` refuse the shadow before anything is created. The shadow keeps its own history in a bare git repo written with plumbing only (`git fast-import`, `ls-tree`, `cat-file`), with an isolated configuration. Commit, revert (a no-op when nothing differs), writes checked against the expected old text, and listing/pruning of old run directories are all in place.
2. The Lean check engine (packages/runner/src/gate/: engine.ts, findings.ts, scratch.ts):
   - `checkBase` builds the user's files before any prompt. Lean errors come back as problems naming file and line; on success the base facts are kept in `<runDir>/base-facts.json`.
   - `check` runs G0 first and starts no Lean when G0 finds something; otherwise it syncs the build copy, builds, and hands core's rules the base, the newest adopt commit and the round start. A build with Lean errors never passes, even if the rules say nothing.
   - `freeze` computes the permitted set and builds the comparator challenge in a copy without the target's `.holds` and everything that uses it, via the new optional `FreezeOptions.removeDecls`.
   - `gate` judges one committed state and runs the comparator only for status proved.
   - `checkGhost` applies the single-term rule before any Lean, makes sure the build copy holds a clean check, then runs the pinned scratch file and reads the axioms only from the message naming `telelean_ghost_check`.
   - `renderStatements` prints the default and explicit forms.
   - Outcome mapping: timeout/oom → `budget` (counted); could-not-start, low memory, cancelled, an unusable working copy, and shadow git errors → `environment` (not counted).
3. Fixtures in test-fixtures/gate/: edit scripts, inert `*.lean.txt` snippets for `sorry` and `#eval`, and overlays (a slow module for the timeout/cancel tests, another subject with a Lean error, a pending promotion, an already-proved derivation).
how_to_run_tests: cd /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/runner && free -m && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json && npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && ulimit -c 0 && TELELEAN_TEST_TMP=<a scratch dir> npx vitest run test/shadow test/gate test/lean test/semantic   (real Lean under runLean; about 160 s; the [gated] blocks in test/gate/rules.test.ts run whenever WP1's core functions are implemented, as they are now)

minor_decisions.decision: Shadow history is a bare repository written with `git fast-import` (the whole snapshot per commit, `deleteall` + inline files) and read with ls-tree and cat-file. There is no index, checkout or work-tree command; revertTo writes the files itself. All `GIT_*` environment variables are dropped, then GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, hooks/excludes/attributes set to /dev/null, an empty init template.
minor_decisions.rationale: A commit is then exactly the judged bytes, and no user git setting, filter, attribute or hook can touch the shadow.

minor_decisions.decision: The `freeze` commit is made only after the challenge export succeeded (the brief listed it before the challenge).
minor_decisions.rationale: A failed challenge must not leave a commit of a passing kind that a give-up revert could land on.

minor_decisions.decision: engine.freeze evaluates the rules without ctx.freeze (always as the state before this freeze).
minor_decisions.rationale: Otherwise an adoption's re-freeze or Accept's re-check would flag the adopted ghost's `.holds` or the user's own axioms as axioms added after a freeze.

minor_decisions.decision: A failing challenge build or export, or any exception while preparing the freeze copy, is an `environment` outcome (not counted).
minor_decisions.rationale: At that point the agent's files have already built and passed the rules, so the failure is telelean's.

minor_decisions.decision: checkBase maps a timeout or oom of the user's own files to `problems` with a `budget` finding ('Your files took too long or too much memory to build …'); sandbox, low memory and cancel map to environment.
minor_decisions.rationale: It is a property of the user's files, and the run must end before any prompt either way.

minor_decisions.decision: The engine adds G1 `build` findings from the facts whenever core's rules report no `build` finding but the build had errors.
minor_decisions.rationale: Fail closed: a gate must never pass Lean errors.

minor_decisions.decision: The gate reuses the head commit when it is a normalise or checkpoint commit with exactly ws/'s files; otherwise it commits a `checkpoint` ('State judged by the gate (round N)'). Other labels: 'Statements frozen (round N)', 'Normalised (round N)'.
minor_decisions.rationale: One judged commit per state, with no duplicates on a repeated finish.

minor_decisions.decision: createRunShadow also refuses symlinks anywhere under `<library>/` (dot-entries skipped, as M1's scan does), symlinked root model or project files, and non-regular on-disk versions of the given files. A symlinked `.lake` or `.lake/build` itself is simply not seeded (M0 behaviour).
minor_decisions.rationale: Makes 'a symlink in the source' concrete while the texts come from the TextSource; a symlinked model file could otherwise pull outside text into what Claude reads.

minor_decisions.decision: Base commit round = 1. commits() returns oldest first.
minor_decisions.rationale: The first round starts from the base.

minor_decisions.decision: The build copy keeps the user's mtime for a source whose text equals the file on disk.
minor_decisions.rationale: Keeps a seeded .lake/build valid. I verified that Lake 4.35 decides rebuilds by content hash: rewriting a source with identical text rebuilds nothing.

minor_decisions.decision: Ghost scratch file: only the statement is whitespace-collapsed; the proof keeps its line breaks, each line indented two spaces. Errors are reported as 'Lean error in the suggested statement / in the proof: …'. aloneEntails = no `.holds` from permitted.selected or permitted.derivationFootprints in the axioms.
minor_decisions.rationale: Collapsing a proof would break tactic blocks; indenting keeps every proof line inside the check theorem.

minor_decisions.decision: RenderedStatement.pretty and .explicit are Lean's whole `#print` message (header and value), from one stdin file with each form on its own line.
minor_decisions.rationale: Matches the type doc '#print of the statement abbrev'.

minor_decisions.decision: Freeze copies keep their sources in frozen/<n>/project but drop their .lake after the export; comparator work dirs are gate/<n>; base facts live in <runDir>/base-facts.json.
minor_decisions.rationale: Keeps run dirs small while leaving what was frozen inspectable.

minor_decisions.decision: checkGhost reuses the last clean check only when it was of exactly ws/'s files and the build copy's model files still equal them. The engine's caches are bounded (32 models, 16 runs).
minor_decisions.rationale: One engine may serve many runs; the content comparison guards against another engine or a direct syncMirror changing the build copy.

open_issues: The [gated] tests are not skipped right now: WP1's functions already exist in the shared tree, and the tests passed against WP1's in-progress code at about 20:48–20:57 and 21:02 local time. The integrator should re-run test/gate/rules.test.ts once WP1 is final.

The freeze copy's removal closure comes from facts refs, so an `example` that uses the target's `.holds` (it has no name) cannot be removed. The challenge build then fails and the freeze is refused as `environment`, with Lean's message. Rare: proof-before-freeze forbids examples before a freeze, so this can only happen in Accept's re-check.
LeanDiagnosticView.column and findings' `file:line:col` use the facts' UTF-16 character. That equals Lean's code-point column except after astral-plane characters.

integration_notes:
For WP3, the RunManager:
- Call engine.checkBase(ctx) right after createRunShadow. It needs a full CheckContext (selection, stage 'formalise', round 1, teleleanBlocks []).
- Pass `roundStartCommit` for round > 1 and for Accept's re-check, and `baseCommit` = the accept-base commit only for that re-check. The engine finds the newest `adopt` commit itself.
- ctx.freeze is ignored by engine.freeze but used by check, gate and checkGhost.
- GateReport.commit is the normalise commit when normalisation changed something, else a checkpoint; commit `gate-pass` with filesAt(GateReport.commit.id).
- GateReport.footprint is present for status proved whenever the facts have T.holds, even when the gate failed.
- environment outcomes: a GateReport with `environment` and no findings, a CheckReport with outcome 'environment', a FreezeOutcome with `environment`, a GhostCheck with `environment`.
- GhostCheck ok always carries `statement` (the collapsed text). When the pre-check fails, `problems` starts with 'The files do not pass check_lean, so the suggestion was not checked. Fix these first:' followed by the finding messages.
- The give-up sentence can use the freeze commit label 'Statements frozen (round N)'.
- pruneRunDirs is the RunManager's to call after a run ends; pass the active run id in `protect`.

For WP4: CheckReport.model and .facts are set whenever Lean ran (ok or problems after the build); renderStatements returns '' plus `error` for names Lean could not print.

ShadowWorkspace:
- commits() returns oldest first.
- currentFiles() throws ShadowLayoutError not-regular or hidden-entry with `paths`.
- writeFiles is all-or-nothing on `before`.
- openRunShadow(runDir, { root, library }) matches RunServices.openShadow.

The challenge module is `<library>.TeleleanChallenge` inside frozen/<n>/project. The fixture edit scripts in test-fixtures/gate/edits.json are anchored on test-fixtures/spyro (WP3's walkthrough scripts may reuse their texts).
